subject: Recap: Ledgerly renewal discussion — qualification for Dedicated pilot and new workloads
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Ledgerly renewal discussion — qualification for Dedicated pilot and new workloads

Hi Ava — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: token costs spiking and unpredictable latency for conversational summarization during peak analysis windows (10–12PM PST).
- Secondary pain: embeddings index refreshes are slow; current infra struggles with concurrent queries from search and similarity features.
- Goal: stabilize latency to <300ms p95 for user-facing summarization, reduce per-token inference cost by ~30%, and enable nightly index rebuilds within a 3-hour window.

Current usage snapshot you shared
- Monthly tokens (gen): ~9.4M; spikes to ~1.2M tokens/day during peak days.
- Embeddings calls: ~480k/month. (Thanks for the Q2 export — attached.)

New/proposed workloads
1) Realtime summarization (low-latency path) — target for rollout to 20% of traffic in Q3.
2) Embedding rebuilds and batched reranking (throughput-heavy nightly jobs).
3) Small-batch interactive queries from the sales portal (bursty).

Recommended path (what we think makes sense)
- Phase A (pilot, 6–8 weeks): Dedicated reserved capacity (2x small GPU nodes) + Redwood Optimize configuration (dynamic batching + prefix caching) to validate latency and cost.
- Phase B (rollout): Move production critical summarization to Dedicated, keep embeddings on managed hosted with scheduled batch windows or add a compute pool if Q3 volumes increase.

Proposed asks for your team
- Confirm target p95 latency and acceptable cost delta for pilot.
- Share the last 30 days of token/embedding logs (we have the Q2 CSV but a rolling 30d helps sizing).
- Stakeholders: loop in Infra lead (you mentioned Daniel) for networking/VPC questions if we go Dedicated.

Next steps
- Rishi will send a pilot sizing + indicative pricing by EOD Tue (22 Jun).
- We propose a 30-min technical kickoff with Daniel and your infra team next week to scope VPC and onboarding timelines.
- We’ll send a short PSR (pilot success rubric) that outlines latency/cost/coverage acceptance criteria.

Attachments: q2_usage_export.csv (token/embeddings snapshot), soc2_summary_excerpt.pdf (requested).

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on the infra contact and the rolling 30d logs.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@ledgerly.com>

Cc: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@ledgerly.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Ledgerly renewal discussion — qualification for Dedicated pilot and new workloads

Thanks Grace — that lines up with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Latency target: p95 < 300ms is correct for the user-facing summarization. For background batch jobs we’re OK with longer windows.
- Cost tolerance: we can accept up to a 25–30% increase in committed spend during the pilot if it demonstrably reduces per-token unit costs and reduces failed requests during spikes.
- Infra: Daniel is cc'd and will own networking/VPC questions. He prefers a short pre-kickoff call to confirm firewall and peering requirements.

We’ll pull the last 30 days of token logs and share as a rolling export by EOD Tue. One ask: can you include an indicative number for how much reserved capacity we’d need to hit the p95 target (ballpark v. exact)? That helps our finance review.

Ava
Ava Simmons
Head of Product
Ledgerly

Grace / Monica — quick internal note with the sizing/pricing approach I mentioned on the call.

Ballpark sizing (based on 30d rolling + peak shape):
- Dedicated pool recommendation (pilot): 2 x a2-high (or equivalent) GPU nodes configured for low-latency mix. This handles the 1.2M tokens/day peak and provides headroom for concurrent embeds.
- Expected steady monthly cost (pilot, reserved 1mo): ~$28k–32k/month (includes reserved compute + network).
- Expected per-token cost delta vs hosted: ~25% lower at steady state once batching/caching tuned.

Pilot design notes:
- 6-week technical validation, with a 2-week observation window.
- PSR: validate p95 < 300ms for user flows, embedding rebuilds complete within 3 hours, and request success > 99.5% during peak.
- Offer: include one month of pilot credits (up to $10k) and a 15% discount on the first 3-month reserved commit if they convert.

Action items:
- Grace: confirm the meeting time for infra pre-kickoff with Daniel.
- Monica: prepare a one-page onboarding checklist (networking, credentials, data handling) and share the DocuSign template for the pilot SOW.

Rishi
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
